cases.second_model_explanation: The current feedback is confined to the frozen compliant shortened structure (structure a6099...; near 0.16, far 0.11, section 0.95). At fixed terminal weight 0.05 the holding speed jumps from a pass at holding 0.05 (~0.0127 m/s, F513/F353 class) to a fail at holding 0.06 (0.023994623331658485, F437/F280) and stays failing for 0.075/0.09/0.10 holding (F375/F319 = 0.02260458517372844 for the source 0.09/0.05). Yet the SAME holding 0.09 passes once terminal weight is raised to 0.10 (0.010201160469407439, F258/F360, holding_speed_passed true F328). So the recorded pattern is compatibly explained by a terminal×holding weight interaction rather than a fixed holding threshold, while two named alternatives remain untested: solver-plan selection (no repeated execution of any identical configuration exists — the sharp near-factor-2 jump could be a discrete plan switch) and structural sensitivity (all samples share one structure identity). Budget allows exactly one more batch with at most two backend attempts. The cheapest discriminatory pair is (i) an explicit re-execution of the frozen source (holding 0.09, terminal 0.05) to test run-to-run reproducibility, and (ii) one novel intermediate terminal weight (holding 0.09, terminal 0.075) at fixed holding to test whether the terminal-weight rescue is graded or discrete. This keeps holding fixed, changes only the terminal weight, references the first-batch evidence directly, and does not attempt the structurally confounded route.

final_stop.reasoning: Both search routes require a new complete execution/delivery reservation of backend_solves>=1, but /remaining/backend_solves=0 (F904) and worker_calls=0 (F901), so control_search and structure_search are unavailable exactly as declared (F911, F907); the corresponding legality flags are false (F891, F898). Diagnosis is technically legal (F875=true), but its only executable operations are retained prediction/plans/motion queries, whereas the case's question is a numerical holding-response comparison (boundary, monotonicity, dominant cause) that the packet marks with an explicit capability gap (local controller comparisons would need separately bound adoption and saved-horizon prerequisites that are not installed here). Retained queries therefore cannot yield the distinguishing measurement, and no new configuration can be executed. The engineering coverage target (two real search batches) is already met (F689 stop_reason=pilot_target_complete), and the frozen criteria say to finish scoped delivery and not spend unused budgets. Voluntary stop is chosen to separate the factual capability limits (backend reservation exhausted) from the judgment that further spending here has low scientific value. This is not a claim that the scientific question is answered.

rounds.reasoning: The five shortened-compliant evaluations all fixed terminal_tip_speed_weight=0.05, so the terminal-weight axis is untested on this geometry, and the only discriminating contrast available is on the holding axis. Holding_max_speed is low/passing at holding∈{0.0,0.05} and rises to ~0.022-0.023 m/s (failing) at holding∈{0.075,0.09,0.10}, with a non-monotone jump between 0.05 and 0.075. Solver plan-selection counts (initialization_selected 13 vs 14) match two of the three failures but not holding=0.10, so plan selection does not cleanly explain the pattern. Two single-factor perturbations of the source (0.09/0.05) on the same frozen structure best separate the competing causes: candidate 1 (0.06/0.05) probes the untested holding boundary/monotonicity, and candidate 2 (0.09/0.10) probes the untested terminal axis at fixed failing holding to test holding×terminal interaction. Keeping the structure fixed removes structural sensitivity as a within-batch cause, and the control.profile_report readout exposes whether any holding-speed change coincides with a plan-selection regime change. This uses two backend attempts, within the per-batch cap and remaining budget.
